newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Forrestania says it finds more nickel.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Forrestania says it finds more nickel.

text.p: Forrestania Gold NL said on Wednesday it has discovered nickel mineralisation at its Roundtop joint venture near the Maggie Hays nickel find in Western Australia.
An intersection of 6.7 metres grading 3.61 percent nickel from a depth of 193.3 metres was recorded, Forrestania said.
Above this zone, the hole also intersected 0.9 metres, grading 4.38 percent nickel from 191 metres, the company said.
The 50/50 Lake Johnston joint venture of Forrestania and Gencor Ltd has 75 percent of Roundtop and Capricorn Resources Australia NL has 25 percent.
Forrestania said the discovery highlights the potential of the Lake Johnston region to host additional nickel sulphide deposits beyond the Maggie Hays deposit.

The mineralisation was hosted by the same ultramafic unit as that which hosts the Maggie Hays deposit and was located in a heavily soil-covered area which until now has only undergone limited drilling, it said.

Forrestania and Gencor are spending about A$8.7 million during the current financial year with the intention of commmencing a bankable feasibility study in the September 1997 quarter on the Lake Johnston joint venture.
The partners are looking to employ Gencor's Bio-nic process, a bacterial method of extracting nickel and gold from sulphide ores, at Maggie hays.
Roundtop is situated about seven km north of Magggie Hays.
